'''Hallard Thomas Croft''' (15 April 1936 – 15 September 2025) was an English mathematician.<ref name="camreporter">{{cite news |title=Obituary Notices |url=https://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/reporter/2025-26/weekly/6796/section7.shtml |access-date=November 18, 2025 |work=Cambridge University Reporter |date=September 24, 2025}}</ref> 

==Life and career==
Born in [[Bromley]], he was educated at [[City of London School]]<ref name=Tel/> and earned a PhD from the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1961, under [[John Edensor Littlewood]]'s supervision.<ref name="mathsgenealogy">{{cite web |title=Hallard T. Croft |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=42565 |website=Mathematics Genealogy Project |access-date=November 18, 2025}}</ref> A fellow of [[Peterhouse, Cambridge]], from 1963 to 2003,<ref name=Tel>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/obituaries/2025/11/21/hallard-croft-cambridge-peterhouse-trevor-roper-dacre/ |title=Hallard Croft, flamboyant Cambridge don who waged war on Hugh Trevor-Roper at Peterhouse |type=obituary |newspaper=Daily Telegraph |date=21 November 2025 |access-date=21 November 2025 }}</ref> in 1967 he invented a geometric shape called Croft's Tortoise and in 1991 he co-authored ''Unsolved Problems in Geometry'' with [[Kenneth Falconer (mathematician)|Kenneth Falconer]] and [[Richard K. Guy]].<ref>{{cite book |author1=Croft, Hallard T. |author2=Falconer, K. J. |author3=Guy, Richard K. |title=Unsolved Problems in Geometry |location=New York |publisher=Springer |year=1991 |isbn= 9780387975061 }}</ref>

Croft clashed with [[Hugh Trevor-Roper]] after the latter became Master of Peterhouse in 1980 when Croft was Director of Studies in mathematics and Senior Fellow;<ref name=Tel/><ref name=Times>{{cite news |title=Hallard Croft obituary: Mathematician in Cambridge feud |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/obituaries/article/hallard-croft-obituary-death-ppzt6nn2j |access-date=November 18, 2025 |work=The Times |date=November 18, 2025|quote=Trevor-Roper, who felt increasingly that his authority as master was being challenged by Croft and his allies, refused to renew his fellowship. Croft's friends suggested this action was motivated, in part at least, by hostility towards his homosexuality.}}</ref> Croft's conservatism led him to deeply dislike Trevor-Roper, and the upshot was that he was re-elected as a Fellow in 1983 without his seniority. Friends suggested that Trevor-Roper disliked Croft because of his homosexuality.<ref name=Tel/><ref name=Times/>
